subject: backswimmer insect
title: This Insect Hovers Underwater Like a Submarine, Using Blood Protein

scenes.text: This insect hovers in midwater, perfectly still, like a tiny submarine.
It's a backswimmer. It swims upside down and ambushes prey from the middle of a pond.
Most water bugs carry an air bubble that makes them float back up.
This one breathes the bubble down, and it should start sinking.
Instead, haemoglobin in its abdomen releases stored oxygen into the bubble, keeping it just right.
Australian scientists filmed over 300 dives. It's the same protein that makes your blood red.

description:
Anisops backswimmers hover in midwater to ambush prey, something air-breathing insects normally can't do.
As their air bubble shrinks, haemoglobin in their abdomen releases oxygen into it, keeping them near neutral buoyancy, as researchers in Adelaide showed across hundreds of filmed dives.
What other animal would you guess uses this trick?
first_comment: The bubble also soaks up oxygen from the water, like a gill. Would you rather hover or swim upside down?
